# Cryptography and Data in Transit (CRY)

## SCS-CRY-01 Encrypt all data in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: All network traffic MUST use TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 with certificate validation, including internal service-to-service, database and SAP traffic. Plain HTTP MUST NOT be allowed in production builds. Certificate validation MUST NEVER be disabled.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Use only https:// base URLs and check this at startup in release builds (fail if the scheme is not https).
- Dart's HttpClient, package:http and dio ignore Android network_security_config and iOS ATS, so enforce HTTPS in Dart. Still ship an Android network security config with cleartextTrafficPermitted="false" for native components.
- Never set badCertificateCallback to return true. For a staging server, give it a publicly trusted certificate; if that is impossible, allow one exact certificate for one host, behind a compile-time flag (--dart-define) that is never set for production.
- iOS: no NSAllowsArbitraryLoads in Info.plist.

Verification: TLS scan of endpoints (for example testssl.sh or SSL Labs for internet-facing hosts). Grep for http://, badCertificateCallback, TrustServerCertificate and ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback.

## SCS-CRY-02 Use only approved algorithms and platform crypto libraries

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Cryptography MUST use approved algorithms through platform or well-maintained libraries: AES-256-GCM (or ChaCha20-Poly1305) for encryption, SHA-256 or stronger for hashing, HMAC-SHA-256 for integrity, and a cryptographically secure random number generator for keys, tokens and codes. Home-made cryptography and broken algorithms MUST NOT be used.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Forbidden for security purposes: MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES, RC2, RC4, ECB mode, and unauthenticated CBC.
- Use a unique nonce for every AES-GCM encryption. Compare secrets and MACs in constant time.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Random values: Random.secure(), never Random().
- Use maintained libraries (for example package:cryptography or platform Keystore/Keychain APIs). Do not write your own cipher code.

Verification: SAST crypto rules (CA5350, CA5351, Sonar weak-crypto rules). Grep for MD5, SHA1, CipherMode.ECB, new Random(, Random().

## SCS-CRY-03 Manage encryption keys securely

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Encryption keys MUST be generated securely, stored in a key management system (Azure Key Vault on the server; Android Keystore / iOS Keychain on devices), never hardcoded, limited to the services that need them, and rotated on a defined schedule and immediately after suspected exposure.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Generate local database keys with Random.secure() and keep them in flutter_secure_storage (backed by Keystore/Keychain). Never in code, assets or --dart-define values.

Verification: Cryptographic inventory exists and shows rotation dates. Grep for embedded keys (-----BEGIN, base64 keys).
